summary: Iteration 9 QA of the new commercial layer: public marketing site, /api/leads capture, admin Leads view, read-only demo auth, plus core-triage regression. BACKEND: new pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_iter9_leads_demo.py (27 cases, run serially with -n 0). 25/27 pass. Verified POST /api/leads (public) returns {ok:true,id}, lowercases work_email, defaults status='New', persists to db.leads (confirmed via staff GET, no _id leak); blank name/work_email/company -> 400 'required'; omitted field -> 422; GET /api/leads unauth -> 401, staff Bearer test_session_step2_demo -> list sorted desc by submitted_at; PATCH /api/leads/{id} accepts New/Contacted/Qualified/Closed with persistence verified via GET, invalid status -> 400, unknown id -> 404, unauth -> 401. Demo auth: POST /api/auth/demo -> user_id 'demo-viewer', is_demo=true, cookie demo_* set HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=None; demo session gets 403 on GET/PATCH /leads, PATCH /issues/{id}, POST /issues/{id}/message, POST /issues/{id}/approve-answer, and 200 on GET /issues, /dashboard, /impact. Triage regression (live Claude): 'What time does the pool close?' -> RESOLVE+resolved+auto_response; "My dishwasher isn't working." -> ACTION+assigned_team; Nathan Brooks/Unit 603 'The sink you fixed is leaking again.' -> matched_existing=true on the SAME issue id, status reopened, failed_resolution=true, zero duplicate 603 issues. FRONTEND (public preview URL): all 7 public routes (/, /product, /pricing, /about, /contact, /privacy, /terms) render with public header (Product/Pricing/About/Contact + Staff Login + View Demo) and footer, correct H1 'Resident requests shouldn't disappear into an inbox.', three lanes RESOLVE/ACTION/REVIEW, Resolution Memory section with red 'PREVIOUS RESOLUTION FAILED' bar, Pricing shows tier-free/tier-standard(MOST POPULAR)/tier-portfolio; no admin notification email string anywhere on public pages; zero page/runtime errors. Contact form: empty submit shows toast 'Please fill in your name, work email and company.' and NO success state; valid submit -> contact-success + success-view-demo. View Demo (header + /staff/login) logs in as demo viewer, lands on /staff, sidebar shows DEMO ENVIRONMENT badge and nav-leads is hidden; attempting a status change in the issue sheet as demo does not change the value (API 403 handled without crash). Real staff session (cookie injection): /staff shows impact-strip (48% / 1.3h / 100% / 3 / 3), impact-snapshot-btn, reset-demo-btn, view-impact-link; nav-leads visible and /staff/leads lists leads with working lead-status-{id} dropdown (New -> Contacted, persisted after reload). Unit 603 issue sheet renders failed-resolution-banner as a strong red-header block with attempts/contacts/original report. /portal resident flow works: submit request -> 'We've got it.' triage card; My Requests tab + track-requests-btn lists the request with status. All test data removed and Unit 603 restored to seed values (21 issues, 50 interactions, 2 leads).

minor.issue: Rate limit is ineffective behind the k8s ingress: request.client.host is the proxy pod IP (observed alternating 10.208.134.66 / 10.208.134.70), so 6 rapid public submissions from one client all returned 200 (limit never hit). Verified the limiter logic itself works when called directly on localhost (6th -> 429). Two problems: (a) abuse from a single real client is not limited, (b) once a proxy IP hits 5, ALL legitimate visitors sharing that proxy IP are blocked. Fix: derive the client IP from X-Forwarded-For (first hop) and/or use a persisted/shared counter instead of the in-process dict _lead_hits (also lost on every reload/restart and not shared across workers).
Email validation accepts an empty local part: work_email='@example.com' was accepted and stored (200). Check for a non-empty local part (or use pydantic EmailStr).
Rate-limit counter is incremented BEFORE validation, so 400-rejected submissions consume a legitimate user's 5/hr quota.
Read endpoint is gated by require_staff_write (works — demo gets 403 — but the dependency name is misleading for a GET; consider require_staff_full/require_non_demo).

ui_bugs.issue: Route is not guarded for demo users: a demo viewer navigating directly to /staff/leads sees the full page shell with the misleading empty state 'No demo requests yet' while the API actually returns 403. Should redirect or show an 'Available to staff accounts only' state.

issues: AuthContext fires /api/auth/me on every public page for anonymous visitors, producing repeated 401s in the browser console (8 observed on the homepage). Cosmetic but noisy for judges opening devtools — skip the call when no session cookie/flag exists.

action_items: POST /api/leads: use X-Forwarded-For for rate limiting (and move the counter out of the in-process dict); currently the documented 5/hr limit never triggers through the public URL and can collectively block real visitors.
POST /api/leads: reject emails with an empty local part ('@example.com' currently accepted); only count rate-limit hits after validation passes.
Guard /staff/leads in the frontend for is_demo users (redirect to /staff or show a not-authorized state) instead of rendering 'No demo requests yet' on a 403.
Optional: suppress the /api/auth/me 401 console noise on public marketing routes.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _lead_hits is process-local and keyed on request.client.host — behind ingress this is the proxy IP; it is both bypassable (round-robin proxies) and a shared-fate DoS on genuine leads. Use the forwarded client IP plus a TTL collection in Mongo.
Lead email validation is hand-rolled ('@' and '.' checks); switch LeadCreate.work_email to pydantic EmailStr for consistent 422/400 behaviour.
server.py is 1686 lines — leads, documents, auth and triage should be split into routers/modules per the 700-line guideline.
Lead notification email is correctly wrapped in try/except and never blocks creation; admin email is only read from LEAD_NOTIFY_EMAIL env and is not exposed in any public UI (verified).

success_rate.backend: 93% (25/27 pytest cases; 2 failures = lead rate limit through proxy + empty-local-part email accepted)
success_rate.frontend: 95% (all flows pass; 1 medium route-guard gap on /staff/leads for demo users)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the iteration-9 suite serially: `pytest tests/test_iter9_leads_demo.py -n 0` (the file restarts the backend via supervisorctl to clear the in-process lead rate limiter; xdist parallelism would race with those restarts). The rate-limit test is EXPECTED to fail until X-Forwarded-For is used. POST /api/issues body field is `name` (not resident_name). Always run restore_603.py and delete extra 603 interactions after any Resolution Memory test.
rca_of_the_issue: Rate limit: create_lead keys _lead_hits on request.client.host, which behind the Kubernetes ingress is the reverse-proxy pod IP. Requests round-robin across at least two proxy IPs, so a single client's 6 submissions split across buckets and never reach the 5/hr threshold; conversely, aggregate traffic from unrelated visitors shares one bucket. Confirmed by direct localhost calls where the 6th request correctly returned 429. Email gap: the check only requires '@' and a dot in the domain, so '@example.com' passes with an empty local part.
